metadata.title: Keep the in-progress AOI drawing above deck data layers
metadata.summary: On the deck.gl engine the shape being drawn for an area of interest rendered underneath the mission's data layers, so placing vertices was guesswork. Deck layers are now anchored below terra-draw's MapLibre layers for the life of a drawing session, and overlay layers with no assigned z-index sort above the mission stack so the committed selection stays visible too.

overview.purpose: The deck.gl implementation of MMGIS's engine-agnostic IMapEngine interface. It owns the maplibre-gl basemap, the deck.gl overlay attached to it, the layer registry, and the terra-draw session used for interactive drawing.
overview.background: In overlay mode the deck.gl `MapboxOverlay` is attached with `interleaved: true`, which means MMGIS data layers and terra-draw's drawing layers are entries in the *same* MapLibre style order — their relative position in that order decides what covers what. deck.gl re-derives that position on every `styledata` event via its `resolveLayers()` routine, and a deck layer with no `beforeId` is pushed to the very top of the style.

keyPieces.name: _syncLayers
keyPieces.description: The single funnel that pushes the layer registry to the overlay (or to Deck in standalone mode).

keyPieces.name: _anchorBelowDrawing
keyPieces.description: New: clones layers with a beforeId while a drawing session is live.

keyPieces.name: _sortLayersByZIndex
keyPieces.description: Re-orders the registry by ascending z-index; array order is deck.gl's draw order.

keyPieces.name: enableDrawing / _stopDrawing
keyPieces.description: Start and teardown of the terra-draw session, shared by the finish and cancel paths.

keyPieces.name: setBasemapStyle
keyPieces.description: Runtime style swap driven by the map:setBasemap API in Map_.js.

explanations.title: Declare getLayer on the basemap
explanations.what: Adds `getLayer` to the structural interface the adapter uses to talk to a mapbox-gl or maplibre-gl map.
explanations.why: The stacking fix has to ask the live style whether terra-draw's layers are currently registered. This interface is hand-written precisely so neither map library is a compile-time dependency, so every method the adapter reaches for has to be declared here first.

explanations.title: Own the terra-draw layer ids
explanations.what: Pins the `td` prefix as an MMGIS-owned constant and derives the id of terra-draw's bottom-most style layer from it.
explanations.why: terra-draw's MapLibre adapter renders the in-progress geometry as five ordinary style layers (`td-polygon`, `td-polygon-outline`, `td-linestring`, `td-point`, `td-point-marker`) and registers the polygon fill first. Anchoring on that first id therefore places the entire drawing stack above the deck layers, not just part of it.

explanations.title: Rank un-indexed layers on top
explanations.what: Introduces a sentinel rank for layers that were never assigned an explicit z-index.
explanations.why: Only the configured mission layer stack (`Layers_.js`) calls `setLayerZIndex`. Plugin overlays such as the AOI selection highlight are added on top of that stack and never get one, so treating "no z-index" as `0` sent them to the bottom whenever anything triggered a re-sort.
explanations.impact: This changes ordering for every un-ranked deck layer, not only the AOI selection — anything added outside the mission stack now sorts above all of it.

explanations.title: Cancel drawing before a style swap
explanations.what: `setBasemapStyle` now ends any live drawing session before handing the new style URL to the map.
explanations.why: A style swap replaces every layer in the style and terra-draw does not re-register its own, so the anchor would be left pointing at an id that no longer exists. maplibre refuses to insert before a missing layer, which silently dropped every data layer on the re-add. Ending the session first flushes the anchor while its target is still there.
explanations.impact: Switching basemaps mid-draw is now a cancel: the in-progress shape is discarded and `drawcancel` fires, so consumers see the session end rather than a shape that quietly stopped tracking.

explanations.title: Pass an explicit terra-draw prefix
explanations.what: `prefixId` is supplied to `TerraDrawMapLibreGLAdapter` instead of relying on the library's default.
explanations.why: The anchor id is computed from this prefix. Setting it explicitly keeps the constant above and the ids actually registered in the style from drifting apart across a library upgrade.

explanations.title: Re-sync layers at session start
explanations.what: `enableDrawing` pushes the layer list to the overlay once the shape is set.
explanations.why: `_syncLayers` is the only place the anchor gets stamped, so without this call the deck layers would not drop below the drawing until some unrelated layer change happened to re-sync.

explanations.title: Drop the anchor when drawing ends
explanations.what: The shared teardown path re-syncs after clearing the active shape.
explanations.why: Both the finish path and the cancel path funnel through here, so ordering returns to normal exactly once regardless of how the session ended — which is the "no layer ends up mis-ordered afterwards" requirement.

explanations.title: Route overlay sync through the anchor
explanations.what: Overlay mode sends the anchored copy of the layer list; standalone mode keeps sending the raw array.
explanations.why: Standalone mode has no MapLibre style and no terra-draw session, so there is nothing to anchor against and nothing to fix.

explanations.title: Anchor deck layers below the drawing
explanations.what: While a session is live and terra-draw's layers are present in the style, every deck layer is cloned with a `beforeId` pointing at the drawing's bottom-most layer.
explanations.why: `@deck.gl/mapbox`'s `resolveLayers()` treats a deck layer with no `beforeId` as belonging to a group anchored at the end of the style and calls `moveLayer` to hoist it there — and it re-runs on every `styledata` event, which terra-draw's own `addLayer` calls fire. Burying the drawing was therefore deterministic, not a race. Giving the layers an anchor puts them in a group that resolves below it instead.
explanations.impact: The clones are per-sync and only exist while drawing; the registry keeps the original instances, so nothing downstream ever sees the `beforeId` prop. The `getLayer` guard is load-bearing — `resolveLayers()` hands the anchor straight to `map.addLayer`, which refuses an anchor that is not in the style.

explanations.title: Sort un-ranked layers above the stack
explanations.what: The z-index sort now ranks a layer with no assigned index at the sentinel rather than `0`.
explanations.why: A live smoke test caught the committed selection sliding behind the data layers after a hide/unhide: unhiding re-applies that layer's z-index, which re-sorts the whole registry and pushed the un-ranked selection to the bottom.
explanations.impact: `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so several un-ranked layers keep their insertion order relative to each other — the last one added still wins.

overview.purpose: Vitest unit suite for DeckGLAdapter, run in a jsdom-ish Node context without ever calling init() — the tests construct the adapter and poke its internals directly.
overview.background: There was previously no coverage of the drawing paths at all. The new block builds a stand-in maplibre map that the real `TerraDrawMapLibreGLAdapter` can run against, so the assertions about layer ids reflect what the library actually does rather than what the adapter assumes.

explanations.title: Cover un-ranked z-index ordering
explanations.what: Two tests around `setLayerZIndex`: an un-ranked layer stays last after a re-sort triggered by an unhide, and layers that do have indices still sort ascending.
explanations.why: The first reproduces the smoke-test regression (hide/unhide re-sorting the registry underneath the committed selection); the second pins the pre-existing ordering contract the sentinel could plausibly have broken.

explanations.title: Fake a maplibre style registry
explanations.what: A hand-rolled map double with just enough surface for `TerraDrawMapLibreGLAdapter` to construct, register its layers, and tear them down, tracking registered ids so `getLayer` answers the way a real style would.
explanations.why: The behaviour under test is "is terra-draw's layer in the style right now", so a double that returns a fixed answer would prove nothing. Because the real terra-draw adapter runs against it, these tests check the anchor id against the library rather than against a hardcoded guess.
explanations.impact: The tests reach into privates (`_isOverlayMode`, `_basemap`, `_overlay`) to skip `init()`, so a rename of those fields breaks the suite without breaking the adapter.

explanations.title: Anchor is applied and stays applied
explanations.what: Checks that starting a session stamps the anchor on every layer, that the id matches what terra-draw actually registered first, and that a layer added mid-draw is anchored too.
explanations.why: "Stays on top while layers are toggled or reloaded" is an acceptance criterion, and mid-draw additions are exactly the case the original bug hit — a new layer with no anchor gets hoisted straight over the drawing.

explanations.title: No anchor when the target is gone
explanations.what: With `getLayer` stubbed to report nothing in the style, a layer added mid-draw syncs without an anchor.
explanations.why: This is the guard that keeps a stale anchor from making maplibre reject the layer entirely. Degrading to today's stacking is the safe failure; refusing to add the layer is not.

explanations.title: Style swap flushes then cancels
explanations.what: Asserts the un-anchored sync lands before `setStyle` is called, and that the swap ends the session with a `drawcancel` carrying the shape.
explanations.why: Ordering is the whole point of the fix in `setBasemapStyle`: the anchor has to be gone before the style wipe removes the layer it points at, so the assertion compares mock invocation order rather than just final state.

explanations.title: Teardown restores plain layers
explanations.what: Ending a session drops the anchor, and the layer registry still holds the original un-anchored instances.
explanations.why: Covers the "stacking is exactly as it was before drawing started" criterion, and confirms the clone-on-sync approach never leaks a `beforeId` back into stored state.
